lesson_title: Flat Does Not Mean Backwards: Reading the Walk to School
hook_text: A distance-time graph goes flat for five minutes. Half the class says the learner walked home. Here is what flat really means.
clip_script: Distance from home up the side, time along the bottom. For the first 10 minutes the line climbs: walking away from home. Then, from 10 to 15 minutes, the line goes flat. Flat does not mean going backwards. Flat means the distance is not changing, and distance not changing means standing still. The learner is in the shop buying a vetkoek. Going back home would be a line coming DOWN towards zero. Then from 15 to 25 minutes the line climbs again: walking on. Five words describe every graph. Up is increasing. Down is decreasing. Flat is constant. Straight is linear, same step every time. Bendy is non-linear. Say the word, say the interval, give a reading with a unit: increasing from 0 to 10 minutes, constant from 10 to 15, increasing from 15 to 25. That is full marks, and it is just reading.
visual_style: A distance-time graph draws itself in three sections on a whiteboard; a cartoon shop appears above the flat section; a red wrong arrow pointing down is struck through; the five shape words stamp in one by one.
pacing: Set up the graph, land the flat-means-still point, then the five words at a steady beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for maxima, minima, and when to draw dots instead of a line.
